hooks.expectedPayoff: Who wrote the letter to the warden signed with Tobias Marrow's name
hooks.notes: Thorne shows Elspeth the letter at the ferry landing (ch1); the boy at the Stavely post office was paid by an old man with a bad cough (ch2); Crane confesses he wrote it (ch3).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Why the barge Margery went down on a clear night with Tobias Marrow aboard
hooks.notes: Crane tells Elspeth and Jonas that Tobias was paid to sink the barge, refused, and was sunk with it (ch3); the ledger and Tobias's letter tell the same story (ch5).

hooks.expectedPayoff: What Absalom Crane wrote in his ferry ledger about the night the Margery sailed
hooks.notes: Crane keeps the ledger under his seat and will not let Thorne read it (ch1); he gives it to Elspeth (ch3); it names three men, one of them Alderman Pask (ch5).

hooks.expectedPayoff: What Tobias Marrow's silver compass, which points a little east of true, comes to mean
hooks.notes: The compass's needle points east of true (ch1); Jonas steers by it on Gorse Hill: if you know how wrong a thing is, you can still steer by it (ch4).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Where the strongbox of Wenlow parish money the Margery carried went
hooks.notes: Thorne says the Margery carried sixty pounds of parish gold that was never found (ch2); Crane says it is under the third flagstone of the abbey chapel (ch3); Elspeth and Jonas dig it up (ch4).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Whether Absalom Crane lives long enough to tell what he knows
hooks.notes: Word reaches Stavely that Crane may not see the week out (ch2); he tells them and dies before midnight (ch3).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Which member of the parish council paid to sink the Margery
hooks.notes: Crane says one of the men is still on the parish council (ch3); the ledger names Alderman Pask (ch5).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Who will row Absalom Crane's ferry after him
hooks.notes: Dying, Crane asks for his oar and Jonas says it is safe in the boat (ch3); Jonas takes the ferry across with Crane's oar (ch5).

hooks.expectedPayoff: What Tobias Marrow's letter in the strongbox says
hooks.notes: Elspeth finds the letter on top of the parish money and does not read it (ch4); she reads it, and it tells the ledger's story (ch5).

hooks.expectedPayoff: Who broke the window of the Marrows' cottage and left boot prints under the sill
hooks.notes: Someone breaks a window at the cottage and takes nothing (ch4); the strongbox is locked in the vestry under guard and the ledger goes to the warden (ch5). Left open on purpose: the book ends before Pask is brought in.
